title: Cap. X: Garissoles (2–3) souls/moral quality; Gualther; Confession Art. 10; Martyr modus
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles Reply 2 stretches beyond 'no one gives what he lacks.' He demands a reason why Adam's soul wore original-justice ornaments, while later souls — not carried along by natural traduction but created when God infuses them — lack those same ornaments from the moment of creation and are led into the body missing the father's first perfection; that lack, he adds, would not have been so if Adam had stayed whole. He forbids a simple appeal to propagation, because souls are not propagated or traduced. He also forbids appeal to nature's rule that the diseased generate the diseased, because the soul is not generated, and yet from the first instant of its being it is stripped of those first benefits. Reply 3: a physical quality that sticks only in flesh (disease, leprosy) is a poor twin for a moral quality such as corruption or original sin. Even if a leper naturally generates a leper, or an elephantiac an elephantiac, it does not follow that moral corruption descending from morally corrupt Adam is from propagation's nature alone, with no regard whatever to imputation. Placeus answers the adornment question at once: a rational soul able to hold justice could not be made by the best God empty of justice and holiness — that is, unjust and unclean. Why posterity's souls are not so adorned when produced? Because unclean Adam could not father a clean child; he begot his like. Why a wolf begets a wolf needs no deep theory; Gualther: wolves generate wolves, so sinner Adam generated sinners; wolf-cubs show wolfish greed by clear marks, and in infants sin likewise puts out its strength before age lets them finish any work. Against the 'souls are not propagated' push: Placeus remembers the public confession, Article 10 — it is not necessary to settle how sin can pass from one to another. Martyr too: the mode is obscure and very hard, so less toil should go there; Scripture teaches most clearly that original sin exists and is transmitted; yield to that truth even when the transfer mode is unknown; do not dispute anxiously what is hard to know and safe to leave unknown. Modest ignorance outranks bold uncertain knowledge. Still, Garissoles's reasoning will not let Placeus rest sober, so he asks point-blank: is hereditary sin naturally propagated or not? Garissoles says yes — clean cannot be drawn from unclean; corrupt Adam begot corrupt; God allowed the blot contracted by the first parents' sin to cling in the seed and flow to posterity. Placeus: so it is; none of us refuse that grant at length; it is most true and the constant orthodox answer against the Pelagians.
pass_b_english: For he adds: 2. Nor is it enough if you say that Adam could not communicate what he had lost, because no one gives what he does not have — because here a reason must be given why Adam's soul was adorned with the ornaments of original justice; and why the souls of his posterity, which are not traduced by natural propagation but are created by God in infusion and infused in creation, lack those same ornaments from their very creation, and so are brought by God into the body destitute of that first perfection of father Adam — which would nevertheless have been otherwise if Adam had persisted in his integrity. For here one must not simply recur to propagation, since souls are not propagated or traduced; nor to the law of nature by which the diseased generate the diseased, because the soul is not generated, and yet from the beginning of its being it is deprived of those first benefits. 3. Because a physical quality inhering in flesh alone, such as disease or leprosy, is not well compared with a moral quality such as corruption or original sin. Nor does it follow that if it is truly natural for a leper to generate a leper, or an elephantiac an elephantiac, one should think it is from the nature of propagation alone, apart from every respect to imputation, that from morally corrupt Adam morally corrupt people likewise are generated. First, as for what he says — that a reason must be given why Adam's soul was adorned with the ornaments of original justice — that reason is ready to hand: for since it was rational and capable of justice, it could not be created by the best God without justice and holiness — that is, unjust and unclean. But why are the souls of his posterity not adorned with the same justice when they are produced? The answer is ready too: because unclean Adam could not generate a clean one; for he begot like himself. What need is there for me to give you a reason why a wolf begets a wolf? For as Gualther says, as wolves generate wolves, so Adam the sinner generated sinners; and as wolf cubs show wolfish greed by no obscure proofs, so in infants also sin then exerts its forces when by age they can yet perform no work. But you say: here one must not simply recur to propagation, since souls are not propagated or traduced. I for my part am not forgetful of our public confession of faith. Article 10: Nor do we think it necessary to inquire how sin can be propagated from one to another. Peter Martyr's words too are excellent, to omit others: The matter, he says, is obscure and very hard; and for that reason I think less labor should be spent on it. For since the word of God most clearly teaches that original sin itself exists and is transmitted to posterity, although we do not understand the mode and reason by which it is transferred, still we must yield to the truth; but on a mode that can be known only with difficulty and ignored without loss, one should not dispute too anxiously. In truth it is clear that there are many things whose manner of production we do not know. Modest ignorance is better than bold and uncertain knowledge. But since the learned man's reasoning will not let us be so sober, I ask: is hereditary sin propagated naturally, or not? It is propagated, he says, because no one can draw what is clean from what is unclean, because corrupt Adam begot corrupt people, because God permitted that blot contracted by the first parents' sin to cling in the seed and flow out to posterity. So it is; and there will be none of us who will not grant all that at great length. That is most true, and constantly asserted by all the orthodox against the Pelagians.
source_text: Addit enim. 2. Nec satis est, si dicas Adamum, quae amiserat communicare non potuisse, eo quod nemo dat, quod non habet, quia hic ratio reddenda est, quare anima Adami justitiae originalis decoramentis ornata fuerit; & quare posterorum ipsius animae, quae non traducuntur propagatione naturali, sed a Deo infundendo creantur, & creando infunduntur, iisdem ornatibus ipsa sua creatione careant, adeoque perfectione illa prima patris Adami destitutae in corpus a Deo inducantur, quod tamen aliter futurum fuit, si Adam in integritate sua perstitisset. Hic enim non est simpliciter recurrendum ad propagationem, cum animae non propagentur, aut traducantur; Neque ad legem naturae, qua morbosi morbosos generant, quia anima non generatur, & tamen ab initio sui esse, privata est primis illis beneficiis. 3. Quia non bene comparatur qualitas physica in carne sola haerens, qualis est morbus aut lepra, cum qualitate morali, qualis est corruptio sive peccatum originale. Neque sequitur, si vere naturale est, ut leprosus leprosum, aut elephantiacus elephantiacum generet, ut putandum sit a sola natura propagationis esse, citra omnem respectum imputationis, quod ex Adam moraliter corrupto generantur homines moraliter itidem corrupti. Primum quod ait, rationem reddendam esse quare anima Adami justitiae originalis decoramentis ornata fuerit, ea ratio est in promptu: cum enim rationalis & capax justitiae esset, creari a Deo optimo expers justitiae & sanctitatis, hoc est, injusta & immunda non potuit. Sed quare posterorum ejus animae eadem justitia, cum producuntur non ornantur? etiam obvia est responsio, quia immundus Adamus mundum generare non potuit: genuit enim sibi similes. Quid opus est, ut tibi ratione reddam, quare lupus lupum gignit? ut enim, inquit Gualterus, lupi lupos generant, ita Adam peccator peccatores genuit: & ut luporum catuli lupinam ingluviem non obscuris argumentis produnt, ita in infantibus quoque peccatum tunc quoque vires suas exerit, quando per aetatem opus adhuc nullum possunt perficere. At inquis, Hic non est simpliciter recurrendum ad propagationem, cum animae non propagentur aut traducantur. Ego vero publicae nostrae confessionis fidei non sum immemor. Art. 10. Nec putamus necessarium esse inquirere, quinam peccatum possit ab uno ad alterum propagari. Praeclara sunt etiam Petri Martyris, ut alios omittam, haec verba. Res quidem, inquit, obscura est, & perdifficilis: eoque minus arbitror de ea esse laborandum. Nam cum peccatum ipsum originis extare, & ad posteros transmitti, verbum Dei luculentissime doceat, quamvis modum, & rationem, qua transferatur non intelligamus, tamen veritati cedendum est: de modo autem qui difficulter sciri, & sine jactura ignorari potest, non nimis sollicite, atque anxie disputandum. Re vera constat, multa esse, quae, quomodo producta fuerint, ignoramus. Praestat modesta ignorantia audaci & incertae scientiae. Sed quoniam nobis per Viri docti ratiocinationem non licet ita sobrie sapere, Peto, an peccatum haereditarium propagetur naturaliter, nec-ne? Propagatur, inquit, quia mundum ex immundo nemo elicere potest, quia corruptus Adam corruptos genuit, quia Deus permisit labem illam a primis parentibus peccato contractam haerere in semine, & ad posteros promanare. Ita est, neque aliquis nostrum erit, qui non totum illud prolixissime largiatur. Hoc sane verissimum est, & adversus Pelagianos ab omnibus orthodoxis constanter assertum.
